To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optical conductivity tensor of the Fe L2-3 edge of Fe3Ox is built from experimental measurements of the linear dichroism and the magneto-optical Kerr effect; the magnetic field angular-dependent X-ray dichroism is well described by spherical harmonics up to the third-order expansion for Fe3+ and up to the sixth-order for Fe2+; and the magnetic field angular-dependence of the X-ray dichroic signals can be used to determine the ground-state properties

the magnetic field angular-dependent X-ray dichroism of a thin film can be described using an expansion of the fundamental spectra on spherical harmonics and that the convergence of the series depends on the details (i.e. spin-orbit coupling) of the ground state.

(1) the optical conductivity tensor is a convenient way to describe X-ray magnetic dichrosim; (2) the angular dependence of X-ray magnetic linear and circular dichrosim is well described by a set of fundamental X-ray absorption spectra expanded on spherical harmonic; and (3) the number of terms required to describe the angular dependence depends on the details (i.e. the ground-state symmetry) of the system in consideration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the magnetic and electronic properties of the iron-based superconductors.
the study of the electronic properties of materials and their relation to the structure.
the development of a procedure to build the full magneto optical conductivity tensor of a system from experimental data and the application of this procedure to the Fe L23 edge of Fe3O 4.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the X-ray absorption spectra of the Fe L2 and L3 edges of Fe3O 4 are described by a set of fundamental XAS spectra expanded on spherical harmonic functions.

the X-ray magnetic linear and circular dichroism at Fe L2, 3-edges of a Fe3O4 thin film can be explained by a combination of the crystal-field effect, the valence-state crystal-field effect and the spin-orbit coupling of both the core and valence states.

the X-ray magnetic linear and circular dichroism of transition metal oxides can be described using a set of spectra expanded on spherical harmonic functions, with the number of terms required depending on the ground-state details of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tensorial approach presented here is a very powerful tool to extract the fundamental properties of a material from the magneto-optical spectra.
we have developed a method that allows us to build an optical conductivity tensor from experimental data.
the X-ray magnetic circular dichroism of the Fe L2-3-edge in Fe3O4 can be described by a single tensor, the optical conductivity tensor.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the optical conductivity tensor is a very useful tool to describe the magneto-optical effects in a magnetic material, and it provides a simple way to connect the measured spectra to the fundamental spectra.
the tensorial approach is a very powerful tool for analyzing X-ray magnetic dichrosim data.

the full magneto- optical response of a magnetic material can be described by the conductivity tensor, which can be obtained from a series of measurements of the X-ray magnetic linear and circular dichroism.
